subject: Clarify: request routing, subprocessors, and jurisdictional scope
messages:
From: Amelia Tran <amelia.tran@mediledger.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick Qs on where requests run and which subprocessors touch data

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Security had a few follow-ups before we can move to procurement:

1) Where do inference requests execute by default for the Hosted API? Are we guaranteed they stay in a single country/region?
2) Which subprocessors (cloud regions, logging/monitoring vendors) receive any part of the request or derived telemetry?
3) If we choose a dedicated pool or private deployment, what changes in the subprocessor list and jurisdiction?
4) What is Redwood's deletion workflow if we ask to purge request data and logs tied to a customer?

We’re trying to map this to our data residency policy and SOC 2 scope. Can you point us to a short summary and any evidence artifacts?

Appreciate it — Amelia
Security & Compliance, MediLedger

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Tran <amelia.tran@mediledger.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-06T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests run and which subprocessors touch data

Hi Amelia — quick answers up front, then a short appendix below with evidence pointers. Looping in Laura (product) and Vivek (infrastructure) for the deeper details.

1) Default routing: For Hosted API customers, requests are routed to the nearest healthy region by latency and cost policy. That means by default requests will execute in the cloud region closest to the client IP unless you set a strict "processing region" preference on your account. When you need residency guarantees (e.g., EU-only), we provide a region lock for the Hosted API that pins inference execution to a single region for all requests in that account.

2) Subprocessors: At a high level, subprocessors that may handle request payloads or metadata include: cloud compute providers (AWS: us-west-2, eu-west-1; GCP: us-central1, europe-west4), object storage (S3/GCS) for model artifacts and checkpoints, and optional observability vendors for traces/metrics. For Hosted API the primary data path is the compute region (where the model executes). Telemetry (sampling of traces/metrics) may be sent to our monitoring stack which uses Datadog (US/EU tenants) and internal aggregators — we can restrict telemetry forwarding when required.

3) Dedicated / Private: With Dedicated, you get committed GPU pools in the region(s) you select; subprocessors narrow to the cloud region and managed networking components associated with that pool. With Private (VPC/on-prem), you control network egress and can opt to keep all processing within your VPC; Redwood only accesses the control plane (and then only over customer-authorized connections). In short: Dedicated reduces the subprocessor surface; Private eliminates Redwood-managed cloud subprocessors from the customer-request execution path when deployed on-prem or in your VPC.

4) Deletion workflow: We have a documented two-step delete: (a) application-layer purge — we delete request payloads and derived artifacts from the serving runtime and caches within the region (typically completed within minutes to hours depending on cache/kv lifetime); (b) audit/log retention purge — logs and aggregated telemetry are retained per account SLA (default 90 days), and upon customer-initiated purge we trigger a cross-region tombstone and background deletion across storage backends. We will provide an idempotent deletion request and a signed certificate of deletion after the full purge completes.

Attached: redwood-regional-subprocessor-matrix.csv (summary), redwood-soc2-evidence-summary.pdf

If you want, Vivek can add the nitty-gritty on encryption/KMS and our exact list of subprocessors per-region. Otherwise, we can set up a 30-minute follow-up.

— Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Tran <amelia.tran@mediledger.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-07T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests run and which subprocessors touch data

Amelia — adding a technical supplement to Connor's high level:

- Execution surface: Inference executes on GPU instances inside a single region for a given request. If the account is not region-locked, routing uses a policy that prefers (1) customer preferred region if set, (2) latency-optimal healthy region, (3) cost-tier fallback. We never fan-out a single request to multiple regions.

- Caching & KV: The runtime uses per-region KV caches for session state (LLM KV cache / prefix cache). These are colocated with the compute instance and not replicated cross-region unless you enable a multi-region failover configuration.

- Subprocessor specifics (examples, per-region):
  * US: AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1) for Hosted; Datadog (us) for telemetry; S3 for model artifact staging.
  * EU: GCP (europe-west4), Azure EU regions where requested; Datadog (eu) or self-hosted telemetry endpoints for EU-sensitive accounts.
  * Note: For customers requiring strict EU-only residency, we run dedicated control plane endpoints in eu-west-1 and can disable telemetry export to US SaaS vendors.

- Encryption & KMS: All requests are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest. Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated (bring-your-own-KMS). For Hosted, we use vendor-managed KMS by default but can enable CMK in specific enterprise contracts.

- Deletion guarantees & timeline:
  * Application purge: immediate invalidation of in-memory caches and removal of queued artefacts within minutes.
  * Persistent storage: object-store deletion completes within 24–72 hours depending on replication queues.
  * Logs/metrics: subject to retention policy; a certified purge request triggers staged deletions and a signed confirmation within 10 business days.

I can share the per-region subprocessor CSV (attached) that lists the exact provider endpoints we use for the next 6 months; it's updated quarterly as we add regions or partners.

Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Amelia Tran <amelia.tran@mediledger.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, MediLedger Security <security@mediledger.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests run and which subprocessors touch data

Thanks, Connor and Vivek — that helps a lot. Two quick follow-ups from Security:

• Can you confirm whether request-level user text (prompt + response) is ever persisted outside the execution region for Hosted API customers that do not opt into multi-region failover? Specifically, backups/replication to logging indexes.

• For the deletion certificate: please include the object manifest IDs and the timeline for each storage class (hot cache vs. cold archives). We’ll need that for our vendor risk team.

We’re happy to schedule a short call to go over the CSV and the SOC2 evidence. If possible, please share the CSV and SOC2 excerpt before the call so our team can pre-read.

— Amelia
Security & Compliance, MediLedger
